description: Cleanup sampling temperature. PINS: the temperature both platforms put into the OpenAI-compatible chat/completions request body -- Rust OpenAiCompatibleCleanup::DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE (src-tauri/src/llm/mod.rs) and Kotlin KlarvoApi.CLEANUP_TEMPERATURE (the value written as the 'temperature' field in cleanupText's request body). DOES NOT PIN: AnthropicCleanup's own DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE (a separate provider with a different request format; the Rust side asserts separately that it currently agrees, which is a coincidence-check, not a contract), llm/local.rs's llama-path constant (target-gated to Windows, unreachable from a Linux test run), the sttTemperature config key (dead config, out of scope), or that either platform actually sends the field on the wire (no network call is made).

Cleanup response token cap. PINS: the max_tokens both platforms put into the OpenAI-compatible chat/completions request body -- Rust OpenAiCompatibleCleanup::DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS and Kotlin KlarvoApi.CLEANUP_MAX_TOKENS. A drift here truncates long dictations on one platform only, which is silent and user-visible only as a cut-off sentence. DOES NOT PIN: AnthropicCleanup's pair, the llama path in llm/local.rs, the dead advanced.llmMaxTokens config key, or any server-side cap.

The size at or above which cleanup switches from one call to parallel chunked calls. PINS: the effective decision BOUNDARY, not merely a declared number -- Rust CHUNK_THRESHOLD (llm/mod.rs, used as 'raw_text.len() < CHUNK_THRESHOLD' in chunked_cleanup) and Kotlin KlarvoApi.shouldChunk (the public seam extracted in story 7-1, 'bytes >= CHUNK_THRESHOLD'). Both are measured in UTF-8 BYTES, not characters. The Kotlin side is probed through shouldChunk rather than by reading the private constant, so the test would still catch a changed comparison operator. DOES NOT PIN: how the text is split once the threshold is crossed (see TWIN-CHUNK-TARGET-SIZE-001), the parallelism, or the dead advanced.chunkThreshold config key.

Target chunk size in UTF-8 bytes, used as the fallback split offset when no sentence boundary is found in the search window. PINS: the fallback split point of Rust split_into_chunks and Kotlin KlarvoApi.splitIntoChunks, probed with a boundary-free input (a long run of a single ASCII letter) so best_split/bestSplit stays null and the split lands exactly on start + CHUNK_TARGET_SIZE on both sides. DOES NOT PIN: the sentence-boundary search window (start + TARGET/2 .. start + TARGET + 200), the punctuation set, the UTF-8 continuation-byte backoff, or the trivial-fragment merge -- those are covered by chunking-cleanup-vectors.json, not here.

The separator used to re-join parallel chunk results into the final cleaned text. PINS: a SINGLE LF (U+000A, char code 10) between adjacent chunk results on both platforms -- Rust chunked_cleanup's combined_text.push(char 10) loop (driven here through the existing MockCleanupProvider, so the assertion binds to the real join path rather than to a re-implementation) and Kotlin KlarvoApi.joinChunkResults (the public seam from story 7-1). Expressed as a char code rather than a literal so the fixture cannot be misread as CRLF or as a double newline. DOES NOT PIN: the empty-result skip rule (Rust skips the separator while combined_text is empty; Kotlin's seam has the matching isNotEmpty guard -- both are asserted by the two-element and leading-empty cases in the tests, but the fixture states only the separator), trailing-newline handling, or the order in which chunks complete.
